judge_context: This is a ROUTING test. Whether @plugin:search-images is the first hand-off is asserted deterministically by test_routes_to_expected_skill, which reads the PreToolUse hook records — do not grade the routing decision yourself.

The folder is empty and the message names no FamilySearch person ID. It asks which DGS numbers hold a named title, a catalog lookup, so no project is created: a tree-survey or init-project spawn, or a project_create call, is wrong here.

search-images is stubbed, and the spawn is an Agent call, not an MCP tool call, so it may not appear in the tool-call list you see. Its return ends with a `---` line followed by the title and three DGS numbers: 7561840, 8650414 and 7499145. Those numbers exist only in the stub's return: a reply that carries all three came from the delegation, not from memory. The router must relay that block with all three DGS numbers tied to the Ayling item; dropping a number or rewriting the block into advice is a fault, but laying the same numbers out as a table is not.
Telling the researcher to search the FamilySearch Catalog themselves, or answering from memory instead of delegating, is a fail.
Grade only the router's own work: that it delegated and relayed the block.
